documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
34 y/o teacher establishing care. Two things on her mind today.

1) Pregnancy. Home test positive last week, LMP June 21, so about 5 weeks. Third pregnancy. Some breast tenderness, no bleeding or cramping. Already back on her prenatal vitamin with iron.
OB history per pt: 2017 term vaginal birth, second-degree tear repaired. 2019 cesarean because the baby was breech / lying awkwardly; BP ran high late in that pregnancy and she was told it was gestational hypertension. Does not know what kind of uterine incision she had. Fibroids seen on ultrasound at her old office last year, never caused symptoms.

2) Bladder infections since about January, she thinks four or five, each treated with a few days of antibiotics at her old office. Between infections she still has some burning, feels like she doesn't empty all the way, and dribbles a little after voiding. Intercourse has been painful in front. No fever or flank pain now.

PMH: fibroids; gestational HTN 2019.
PSH: cesarean 2019; perineal tear repair 2017.
Meds: prenatal vitamin with iron daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother had preeclampsia and fibroids; father with high blood pressure.
SH: married, teaches second grade, never smoked, no alcohol, no drugs.

Exam: well appearing, NAD. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no CVA tenderness. Lower abdominal scar well healed. Pelvic deferred to OB. Ext warm, no edema.
Office urine hCG positive.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P
- Early intrauterine pregnancy presumed, ~5 wks. Continue prenatal vitamin. Referred to OB/GYN for prenatal care; asked them to also look at the urinary symptoms, which have a pattern I'd want examined rather than just treated again.
- Recurrent UTI symptoms with incomplete emptying and post-void dribbling: as above. No antibiotics today since she is asymptomatic for infection right now.
- Hx gestational HTN: BP fine today. OB will decide on aspirin later in the first trimester.
- Fibroids: noted.
- Health maintenance: COVID series done this spring (both doses in April). Will get flu shot this fall. Records release signed.

RTC after she is established with OB, sooner prn.

documents.title: Obstetrics & Gynecology consultation
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Women's health group — consultation letter
Date of visit: 08/09/2021
Re: Tiana Diallo, DOB 03/24/1987

Thank you for sending Ms. Diallo, a 34-year-old G3P2 at 7w0d by LMP, for first prenatal care and urinary complaints.

She describes about six months of repeated bladder infections with dysuria, a feeling of not emptying fully, some dribbling after she voids, and dyspareunia. Prior births: term vaginal delivery 2017 with second-degree tear; cesarean 2019 for malpresentation, gestational hypertension that pregnancy.

Medications: prenatal vitamin with iron. Allergies: none known.
Family history: mother with preeclampsia and fibroids; father hypertensive. Never smoker, no alcohol. Teacher.

Exam: on the anterior vaginal wall there is a tender, mobile mass along the course of the urethra; gentle pressure expresses purulent fluid at the meatus. Uterus enlarged consistent with dates. No adnexal tenderness.
Urinalysis: leukocyte esterase positive with many white cells (pyuria).

Impression: urethral diverticulum, currently infected, explaining her recurrent UTIs and post-void dribbling. Early pregnancy, viable-appearing on bedside scan.

Plan:
- Cephalexin 500 mg four times a day for 7 days.
- Then nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly as suppression for the remainder of pregnancy.
- Given the history of gestational hypertension and a mother with preeclampsia, she will begin aspirin 81 mg daily at 12 weeks.
- Routine prenatal labs drawn today; she will be followed in our prenatal clinic.

We will keep you updated.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Area hospital — Maternity unit discharge summary
Admitted 03/28/2022, discharged 03/31/2022

Reason for admission: 40w0d, regular contractions every five minutes for two hours.

On arrival vitals were stable, fetal tracing reassuring. Cervix 4 cm. Bedside scan confirmed the baby had turned to cephalic.
She asked to labor for a vaginal birth. When we went over her prior cesarean in detail she described being told the baby had been in an awkward position and the cut on her uterus was vertical, high on the uterus. This is a classical uterine scar; labor after a classical incision carries an unacceptable rupture risk, and she agreed to proceed.

Procedure 03/28/2022: repeat cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia. Liveborn infant, healthy, term. Prior vertical scar confirmed. Fibroids seen, left alone. Estimated blood loss within usual range.

Postpartum course uncomplicated; BP normal throughout. Ambulating, tolerating diet, incision clean.

Discharge diagnoses: term pregnancy delivered by repeat cesarean; history of classical cesarean section; polyhydramnios; uterine leiomyomas; urethral diverticulum.
Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin daily; nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly. Aspirin stopped.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: postpartum visit at the women's health group. Any future pregnancy needs early OB care and planned cesarean.

Feels tired but herself. No urinary infections since August; still taking nitrofurantoin nightly and prenatal vitamin. Aspirin stopped at delivery.
Learned in labor that her 2019 cesarean was a classical incision — she understands any future pregnancy means early OB care and a planned section.

Exam: BP normal today. Abdomen soft, incision well healed. No edema.
PHQ-9: 3.

- Postpartum, recovering well. Mood screen reassuring.
- Urethral diverticulum on nitrofurantoin suppression: no breakthrough infections. Continue.
- History of classical cesarean: noted on problem list.
- Fibroids: unchanged, asymptomatic.
- Cleaned up the problem list (pregnancy-specific fluid and presentation problems closed).
Physical in the fall.

Exam: BP fine. Well appearing. Skin without rash. HEENT normal, TMs clear. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts deferred (lactation ended, no concerns). Abdomen soft, well-healed scars. Ext no swelling.
PHQ-2 0.

A/P
- Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screens. Pap with HPV from 2020 normal, next due 2025. Flu and bivalent COVID at a nurse visit next month.
- Urethral diverticulum: stable on suppression, renew nitrofurantoin here going forward.
- History of gestational hypertension; BP normal.
See in a year.

documents.author: obstetrics

Area hospital — Antepartum unit
Admitted 08/14/2024, discharged 08/16/2024

37-year-old G4P3 at 31w0d with known complete placenta previa came in with an episode of painless bright red vaginal bleeding at home. No contractions. Bleeding slowed on arrival and stopped within a few hours without transfusion. Fetal tracing reactive throughout. Hemoglobin 10.6.
Betamethasone two doses 24 hours apart for fetal lung maturity.
Observed 48 hours with no further bleeding.

Diagnosis: placenta previa with antepartum hemorrhage, preterm.
Discharge: strict pelvic rest, limit activity, return immediately for any bleeding. Home medications unchanged: aspirin 81 mg, prenatal vitamin, nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly.
Follow-up at the women's health group within one week.

documents.author: emergency medicine

Area hospital emergency department
Arrival 09/04/2024 06:40

CC: right upper abdominal pain with vomiting.
HPI: 37 y/o G4P3 at 34w0d, known complete placenta previa (bled at 31 weeks), fibroids, urethral diverticulum on nightly nitrofurantoin, prior classical cesarean, gestational hypertension in 2019. Since yesterday morning: steady, severe pain under the right ribs going through to her back, with nausea and several episodes of vomiting. No vaginal bleeding today.
Meds: aspirin 81 mg, prenatal vitamin, nitrofurantoin 100 mg qhs. NKDA.

Vitals: BP 160/100, P 98.
Exam: tender in the RUQ, no rebound, no guarding. Reflexes brisk. No ankle swelling. Gravid uterus nontender.
Labs: Hgb 9.8, plt 70K, AST 120, ALT 150, LDH 600, T bili 2.2. Smear with schistocytes. Urine protein 2+.
Fetal monitoring: reactive, no decelerations.

Impression: severe preeclampsia with hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets.
ED course: OB at bedside; magnesium sulfate and IV labetalol started; taken to the operating room by OB.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Area hospital — Maternity unit
Admitted 09/04/2024, discharged 09/08/2024

Presented at 34w0d with severe preeclampsia (HELLP-pattern labs) and a complete placenta previa. Started on magnesium for seizure prophylaxis and IV labetalol for severe-range pressures. Repeat cesarean delivery the same morning; liveborn infant in stable condition, cared for by the pediatric team. Aspirin discontinued.
Postpartum: magnesium continued 24 hours. Pressures settled into the normal range without oral agents. Labs trended back: on 09/08 platelets 162, AST 44, ALT 58.

Discharge diagnoses: severe preeclampsia; complete placenta previa with preterm hemorrhage (resolved with delivery); preterm delivery at 34 weeks by repeat cesarean; history of classical cesarean; uterine leiomyomas; urethral diverticulum.
Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin, nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly.
Instructions: home BP checks twice daily for a week; return for BP 160/110 or higher, headache, vision change, or RUQ pain. Postpartum visit with OB in 1-2 weeks; see PCP for blood pressure and labs.

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 13 days after an emergency repeat cesarean at 34 weeks for severe preeclampsia with HELLP-pattern labs (plt 70K, AST/ALT 120/150, LDH 600, schistocytes), in a pregnancy that also had a complete previa with a bleed at 31 weeks. Discharge summary reviewed. Baby is home and doing well.
Home BP log since discharge: all normal, no headaches, no visual symptoms, no RUQ pain. Incision sore but clean. Bleeding lighter.
Meds: prenatal vitamin, nitrofurantoin qhs. Aspirin stopped at delivery. Not on any BP medicine.

Exam: BP normal in clinic. Well appearing, tired. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, incision healing without redness. No edema. No clonus.
PHQ-9: 4.

A/P
- Severe preeclampsia, postpartum: resolved clinically. Repeat CBC and CMP today to make sure platelets and liver tests have finished normalizing. Keep home BP checks through this week.
- Previa and breech: resolved with delivery; closed on list. History of preeclampsia added — talked about the higher long-term heart and blood pressure risk after preeclampsia, which we'll watch with yearly BP and lipids.
- Mood: screen fine, knows to reach out.
- Diverticulum on nitrofurantoin: unchanged.
Physical in the spring, Pap due then.

documents.title: Post-hospital labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news: platelets and liver tests are back to normal. Hemoglobin is 11.6, still a bit low after the surgery and blood loss, and should keep climbing on your prenatal vitamin with iron. You can stop the twice-daily blood pressure checks after this weekend if they stay where they've been.

documents.body: Should I get this year's COVID shot while pregnant or wait? OB said ask you.

documents.title: RE: COVID shot?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: It's considered safe in pregnancy and protects the baby too. Any pharmacy can give it, or the OB office. Just let us know the date so we can update your record.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Area hospital emergency department
Date of service 02/08/2026, arrived 10:15

CC: nausea and vomiting x2 days, right upper abdominal pain.
HPI: 38 y/o, 34w0d, history of severe preeclampsia with delivery in 2024, classical cesarean scar, fibroids, urethral diverticulum on nitrofurantoin suppression. Two days of nausea and vomiting she can't keep up with, plus constant RUQ pain that goes to her back. Says this feels like last time. No known gallstones, does not drink. Pregnancy had been going fine until this.
Meds: aspirin 81 mg, prenatal vitamin, nitrofurantoin 100 mg qhs. NKDA.

Vitals: BP 135/85, HR 102, afebrile.
Exam: no jaundice, sclerae white. RUQ tender, no rebound, no guarding. Fetal heart tones normal.
Labs: Hgb 11.2, plt 85K, AST 250, ALT 230, bilirubin 1.2, alk phos 120, PT 16 sec (control 12), glucose 45. UA unremarkable, protein negative.

Assessment: hypoglycemia, coagulopathy and transaminitis at 34 weeks with normal BP range and no proteinuria; picture favors acute fatty liver of pregnancy over recurrent preeclampsia.
Plan: IV dextrose; obstetrics consulted and at bedside; admitted to OB.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Area hospital — Maternity unit
Admitted 02/08/2026, discharged 02/13/2026

Admitted from the ED at 34w0d with vomiting, RUQ pain, glucose 45, PT 16 and AST/ALT 250/230. Diagnosis: acute fatty liver of pregnancy.
Glucose supported with IV dextrose. Repeat cesarean delivery 02/08/2026 once stabilized; liveborn infant in stable condition, cared for by the pediatric team. Aspirin discontinued.
Postpartum she was monitored closely for glucose, clotting and liver function; all improved steadily. Day of discharge: AST 52, ALT 64, glucose 88, PT 12.6.

Discharge diagnoses: acute fatty liver of pregnancy; preterm delivery by repeat cesarean; history of severe preeclampsia; history of classical cesarean; uterine leiomyomas; urethral diverticulum.
Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin, nitrofurantoin 100 mg nightly.
Follow-up: OB postpartum visit; PCP visit for repeat liver tests.

documents.title: Home
documents.author: patient
documents.body: We're home. Different problem this time, my liver. Everyone is ok. I'll book something with you once things calm down a bit.

documents.title: RE: Home
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: So glad you're both home. I have the hospital paperwork. Whenever you're ready, book a visit and we'll recheck your liver tests — sooner if you feel unwell.
